stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: A flat transmission spectrum, one showing no absorption features, was long read as evidence that an exoplanet lacks an atmosphere. Astronomers now recognize that a high-altitude aerosol layer, such as photochemical haze or silicate cloud, can produce the same flat spectrum by blocking starlight before it reaches the gases below. Photochemical hazes are thought to form only on planets cooler than about 850 K, while silicate clouds are thought to condense only on planets hotter than about 1,300 K. The planet Veyra-4b has a flat spectrum and a temperature of about 1,050 K, so ______
choices: its flat spectrum is better explained by silicate clouds than by the photochemical hazes found on cooler planets.
it must lack an atmosphere, since both kinds of aerosol layer have been excluded as causes of its flat spectrum.
neither of the two aerosol layers described is a likely source of the flatness in its spectrum.
planets with temperatures between 850 K and 1,300 K are less likely than other planets to retain atmospheres.
explanation: You need three facts at once. At 1,050 K, Veyra-4b is above haze's ceiling of 850 K, so haze is unlikely. It is also below the 1,300 K floor for silicate clouds, so those are unlikely too. Put together, neither named layer accounts for the flat spectrum. That is as far as the chain goes. Haze and silicate cloud are given only as examples ('such as'), and the temperature limits are only 'thought' to hold. So the passage supports ruling out these two layers. It does not support any conclusion beyond that.

A.why: You used only half the chain. You saw that 1,050 K is too hot for haze and stopped there, so you never checked the silicate-cloud threshold. Those clouds condense only above 1,300 K, so the planet is too cool for them as well.

B.why: You got the key point that both layers are ruled out, then took one extra step. The passage gives haze and silicate cloud only as examples ('such as'), so other aerosols aren't excluded. The thresholds are also only 'thought' to hold, so 'must' claims more certainty than the passage gives.

D.why: You went from one planet to a claim about a whole temperature range. The passage says nothing about how often planets in that range keep their atmospheres. It doesn't even establish that Veyra-4b has lost its own.

stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?
stimulus: Traffic-safety campaigns usually judge a street by how often collisions occur on it. A study of twelve residential streets in the city of Ardell, however, found that cutting the speed limit from 30 to 20 miles per hour left the number of collisions essentially unchanged while sharply reducing the share that caused serious injuries. Separately, city hospital records show that collisions causing serious injuries account for most of the traffic-related admissions to Ardell's trauma wards. Taken together, these findings suggest that lower speed limits on residential streets ______
choices: would reduce trauma-ward admissions chiefly by making collisions on those streets less frequent.
could reduce traffic-related trauma-ward admissions even without making collisions any less frequent.
would cut Ardell's traffic-related trauma-ward admissions by more than half within a few years.
would lower trauma-ward admissions more than any other safety measure Ardell has tried.
explanation: The term the two facts share is serious-injury collisions. The total number of collisions stayed the same while the share that were serious fell, so the number of serious-injury collisions fell. Those collisions cause most traffic-related trauma admissions. Chaining the two facts, lower limits could reduce those admissions even though collisions are no less frequent. 'Could' fits the passage's 'suggest'. The choice also keeps the part of the finding that held steady: the number of collisions didn't change.

A.why: You linked lower speed limits to fewer admissions but credited the wrong half of the split finding. The study says the number of collisions was essentially unchanged. Only how severe they were changed.

C.why: You combined 'most' and 'sharply' into a specific figure. The passage gives no amount for either, no timeline and no citywide results; the study covered only twelve streets. 'Suggest' supports only a possible reduction, not a measured one.

D.why: You went past the chain to a comparison no one made. The passage never mentions any other safety measure, so it can't support a ranking.
